name: mise
tagline: A Rust tool for managing development tools, environment variables, and project tasks.
hook: A development guide to registry acceptance, version resolution, Windows paths, deprecations, dependencies, and release notes.
summary: Mise's guide covers registry acceptance, development commands, version resolution, Windows PATH handling, deprecations, and dependency updates. It also explains how pull-request text becomes release-note input.

techniques.title: Name the domain assumption that breaks generic helpers
techniques.body: Date versions, channels, language-specific prereleases, and tool-defined latest values defeat a universal semver comparator. Resolution belongs to backend methods; lockfile versions remain opaque.
techniques.quote: **Do not assume tool versions follow semver or any other orderable scheme.**

techniques.title: Offer a supported alternative to a rejected contribution
techniques.body: The registry section requires evidence of popularity and maintenance for new shorthands. It also explains that explicit backend syntax already installs unlisted tools, separating registry acceptance from product capability.
techniques.quote: The registry is *only* for shorthand convenience for popular tools — not for enabling installation.

techniques.title: Test PATH behavior beyond its rendered shape
techniques.body: Windows rules keep PATH native until an assignment is emitted into a positively identified emulator shell. Verification must execute through that PATH and inspect a native grandchild, rather than only matching a string.
techniques.quote: Windows activation tests must execute a command through the emitted PATH and verify a native Windows grandchild receives a valid semicolon-delimited PATH. Output-shape assertions alone are insufficient.

techniques.title: Tie removal to the start of user warnings
techniques.body: Deprecation normally warns immediately and removes after twelve months. A delayed warning is reserved for migrations that older supported clients cannot parse, and it moves the removal clock with it.
techniques.quote: If a compatibility window is required, removal remains 12 months after `warn_at`, not 12 months after the initial documentation notice.

techniques.title: Unblock wrapper failures without weakening the check
techniques.body: When the transparent Cargo cache wrapper fails, the guide permits the equivalent command with the wrapper disabled. A successful bypass becomes diagnostic evidence to report, while permanent disabling is prohibited.
techniques.quote:
Do not permanently disable the wrapper,
and do not post externally without user authorization.

techniques.title: Treat PR prose as input to another product surface
techniques.body: Release notes come from pull-request titles and descriptions. Rewrite them when scope changes, and make behavior, examples, and adoption clear without the diff or screenshots.
techniques.quote:
Communique uses PR titles and descriptions to generate release notes. Write them
for a mise user who has not read the diff or this conversation.

steal: Call out version formats that defeat generic ordering.
Offer a supported path when a contribution is out of scope.
Test shell behavior through real child processes.
Start deprecation removal clocks from user-visible warnings.
Provide an equivalent check when a cache wrapper fails.
Write PR descriptions for their downstream release-note audience.
